newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thakral says Sing-dlr listing delayed.
newsitem.headline: Thakral says Sing-dlr listing delayed.

text.p: The plan of consumer electronic products distributor Thakral Corporation to convert its share trading in Singapore to Singapore dollars from U.S. dollars has been delayed, a company official said on Tuesday.

"The conversion to Singapore dollar is not going to happen as fast as we initially thought it would be six months ago," Elie Baroudi told Reuters during its announcement of its financial results for year ended March 31, 1997.

"It is not going to happen in the next few months," he said. Baroudi, the company's deputy chief executive officer, said the group needed to extend its Operational Headquarters (OHQ) status conferred by the Economic Board (EDB) of Singapore to 10 years from five years.
An OHQ status gives a concessionary corporate tax rate of 10 percent for the initial period of five years.
Baroudi said Thakral was still talking withthe EDB on how to achieve the extension.
He said the group had set up a treasury and finance centre in Singapore, a requirement for the conversion.
It would also be able to book 35 percent of its net expenditure in Singapore, another conversion requirement. Currently, only six to seven percent is booked in Singapore.
Baroudi said the interest expense from Thakral's US$250 million revolving credit facility with 17 Singapore-based banks would aid this.
